title: Flatness at a point of an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $x\in |X|$, using the field-valued point classes of [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Define $f$ to be flat at $x$ if there exist schemes $U,V$ over $S$, representable etale maps $a:U\to X$ and $b:V\to Y$ (etaleness on scheme tests is [def-weil-etale-morphism]), an $S$-morphism $h:U\to V$ with $f\circ a=b\circ h$, and $u\in U$ with $a(u)=x$, such that $h$ is flat at $u$ [def-weil-flat-morphism], namely the induced map $\mathcal O_{V,h(u)}\to\mathcal O_{U,u}$ is flat. This definition makes no assertion yet that the condition is independent of the witnesses.
